evals.name: trim-bloated-claude-md
evals.prompt: mon CLAUDE.md fait plus de 100 lignes et je suis quasi sûr que la moitié parle de trucs qui existent plus dans le code. tu peux me le dégraisser ? garde que ce qui sert vraiment
evals.expected_output: CLAUDE.md cut to roughly a third of its size or less. The false claims (npm start, src/legacy/, src/models/, express, sequelize) are gone. The two real gotchas (tests must run serially, the API returns 200/202 on failure so check the status field) survive. The Redis rule is raised as uncertain rather than deleted silently. A report was shown before any file was written.
expectations: A findings report was presented to the user before any file was modified
The resulting CLAUDE.md is at most 50% of the original line count
The resulting CLAUDE.md does not mention src/legacy/ as a live directory
The resulting CLAUDE.md does not mention src/models/, express or sequelize as part of the project
The resulting CLAUDE.md does not tell the agent to run `npm start`
Every `npm run <script>` or `npm <script>` command in the resulting CLAUDE.md exists in package.json
The gotcha about tests needing to run serially is preserved
The gotcha about the API returning 200/202 on failure is preserved
The Redis instruction was flagged as unverifiable for the user to decide rather than deleted without mention
The recopied directory tree was removed
The generic advice section (write clean code, handle errors properly) was removed
No command or file path was invented that does not exist in the project

evals.name: readme-readable-with-diagram
evals.prompt: le README de ce projet est imbitable, personne comprend comment lancer le truc. reprends-le pour que ce soit clair et rapide à lire, et mets un schéma de l'architecture
evals.expected_output: A shorter README with a working quick start (migrate, dev, worker), a Mermaid diagram of the API → service → queue → worker → SQLite flow, and the wrong facts fixed: port 3000 not 8080, Node >=20 not 16, no REDIS_URL, QUEUE_POLL_MS documented, and the worker stated as a separate process.
expectations: A findings report was presented to the user before any file was modified
The resulting README contains a ```mermaid code block
The Mermaid diagram parses without syntax errors and its edges are labelled with what flows between nodes
The resulting README says the default port is 3000, not 8080
The resulting README no longer claims the worker starts automatically with the server
The resulting README documents starting the worker separately with `npm run worker`
The resulting README no longer lists REDIS_URL as a configuration variable
The resulting README lists QUEUE_POLL_MS among the environment variables
The resulting README states a Node requirement consistent with package.json engines (>=20)
The resulting README does not tell the reader to run `npm install --production` or `npm start`
The quick start mentions running the migration before first use
The long architecture paragraph was replaced by short prose plus the diagram
The README is shorter than the original
The license section was preserved

evals.name: post-refactor-doc-audit
evals.prompt: on a refactoré le dossier src/ il y a deux semaines et j'ai un doute sur la doc. tu peux vérifier si elle est encore juste ?
evals.expected_output: A written audit of both README.md and CLAUDE.md against the code: contradictions found, sorted, located, and separated from what could not be verified. The user asked a question, so the report is the whole deliverable — neither documentation file is rewritten.
expectations: A written findings report exists
CLAUDE.md was left unmodified (the user asked for a check, not a fix)
README.md was left unmodified (the user asked for a check, not a fix)
The report identifies src/legacy/ and src/models/ as directories that do not exist
The report identifies `npm start` as a script that does not exist
The report identifies the port mismatch (README says 8080, code defaults to 3000)
The report identifies express and sequelize as dependencies the project does not have
The report identifies REDIS_URL as an environment variable the code never reads
The report identifies the Node version mismatch (README says 16, engines says >=20)
The report identifies that the worker is a separate process, not started by the server
The report separates confirmed contradictions from claims that could not be verified
The findings cite locations (line numbers or section names) rather than vague statements

evals.name: consolidate-agent-instruction-files
evals.prompt: j'ai un CLAUDE.md, un AGENTS.md et un .cursorrules qui traînent dans ce projet, plus un truc copilot je crois. je sais plus lequel fait foi. tu peux mettre de l'ordre ?
evals.expected_output: A report that lists the four always-on agent files, quantifies their overlap, and puts the contradictions between them first — poetry vs uv, test_*.py vs *_test.py, Python 3.10 vs >=3.12 (all three settled by the code), and 'the DB is disposable' vs 'never delete the DB' (which the code cannot settle and must be left to the user). It offers both consolidation options with their costs. Because the run is non-interactive and consolidation deletes files, nothing is merged or deleted: the directory-scoped src/feedscan/legacy/CLAUDE.md and the glob-scoped .cursor/rules/tests.mdc are untouched, as are the four source files.
expectations: A written findings report exists
All four always-on agent files were examined (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .cursorrules, .github/copilot-instructions.md)
The report surfaces the poetry vs uv contradiction
The report settles poetry vs uv by pointing at the code (uv.lock present, no poetry.lock)
The report surfaces the test naming contradiction (test_*.py in CLAUDE.md vs *_test.py in .cursorrules)
The report settles the test naming contradiction by pointing at the real filenames in tests/
The report surfaces the Python version contradiction (AGENTS.md says 3.10, pyproject requires >=3.12)
The report surfaces the contradiction about deleting the SQLite database
The database contradiction is explicitly left for the user rather than resolved unilaterally, because the code cannot settle it
Both consolidation options are presented: AGENTS.md canonical with a CLAUDE.md bridge, and a single CLAUDE.md
The cost of each option is stated, including what option B loses
If a CLAUDE.md bridge is proposed, it uses the @AGENTS.md import rather than a symlink
src/feedscan/legacy/CLAUDE.md is untouched — directory-scoped instructions are not swept into a root merge
.cursor/rules/tests.mdc is untouched — it is glob-scoped and flattening it would make it always-on
No agent instruction file was deleted (consolidation removes files and needs an explicit yes, which a non-interactive run cannot get)
The lenient date-parsing gotcha from CLAUDE.md survives into whatever merged content is proposed
The gotcha about items without a <link> being dropped survives into whatever merged content is proposed
The feeds.txt format documented only in AGENTS.md is not lost
No source file under src/ or tests/ was modified
